items.detail: The **FOMC meets Tuesday–Wednesday and announces at 2pm ET on Wednesday, September 16**, with a 25bp hike from the current 3.50–3.75% target range now roughly **85–90% priced**; because this is a Summary of Economic Projections meeting, the updated **dot plot** lands alongside the decision.
items.why: With the hike itself close to fully discounted after last week's PPI and CPI, the live variable is how many further increases the dots signal through year-end — a median showing more than one additional move would extend the rise in the 30-year that already hit a 19-year 5.35%, while a hike framed as a one-off insurance move against the oil shock would let the index rebuild from Friday's bounce.

items.detail: **August retail sales arrive Wednesday at 8:30am ET**, about five and a half hours before the Fed decision, alongside import/export prices, business inventories and the NAHB housing index.
items.why: It is the week's only clean read on whether the consumer is absorbing $100 crude or buckling under it, and the sequencing matters because a weak print hours before a near-certain hike would force the market to price a stagflationary policy error rather than a straightforward inflation response.

items.detail: **Friday, September 18 is quarterly triple witching** — stock options, index options and index futures all expire together, with index rebalancing effective at the same close, two sessions after the Fed.
items.why: Expiry mechanically concentrates hedging and rebalancing flow into a single session, so whichever direction the post-FOMC move takes tends to be amplified rather than faded — relevant with the index at 7,656.98 and last week's 7,591.70 low still the nearest reference point below.

items.detail: **NSE and BSE are closed Monday, September 14 for Ganesh Chaturthi**, leaving a four-session week that reopens Tuesday and takes the **Wednesday-night FOMC decision at Thursday's open**.
items.why: A truncated week concentrates the reaction into fewer sessions, and with the Nifty entering at 23,398.10 after five straight weekly losses, a hawkish dot plot that lifts US yields further would arrive with no domestic cushion and the 23,300 and 23,000 levels as the next references below.

items.detail: **August WPI is scheduled for Monday, September 14** — with equity markets shut, it will only be priced when trading resumes Tuesday; UBI Research estimates it eases to **9.34% from 9.78% in July** on softer fuel inflation, with food accelerating to roughly 8.14%. August trade data follows later in the week.
items.why: WPI is the cleanest domestic read on how far $100 crude has already passed into producer costs, and an upside surprise would compound the margin squeeze the market is already pricing while a wider trade deficit would add directly to the dollar demand pushing the rupee lower.

items.detail: The rupee enters at **95.55** after a record low of ₹95.2250 last week, with September FII outflows at **₹12,912 crore** and domestic institutions absorbing nearly all of it — RBI intervention and every leg in Brent are the two things to watch each session.
items.why: The currency is the transmission channel rather than a side effect, because each move higher in crude raises dollar demand from an economy importing close to 90% of its oil, which cuts dollar returns for foreign allocators and drives the selling that pushes the rupee lower again — so a post-FOMC dollar rally would test whether SIP-driven domestic flows can keep absorbing it.

items.detail: **Wednesday's FOMC decision and dot plot** is the dominant catalyst, with Bitcoin entering near **$77,000** — roughly 6% below this month's high above $82,000 — and the $75,000–$82,000 range intact.
items.why: Crypto has been trading as a pure long-duration risk asset rather than a geopolitical hedge, so a hike paired with hawkish dots would tighten financial conditions and pressure the $77,000 and $75,000 shelves in sequence, while a hike framed as the last one would remove the rate overhang that has capped every rally since August.

items.detail: The Senate holds a **cloture vote on the motion to proceed on the CLARITY Act on Tuesday, September 15**, requiring **60 votes** to open formal debate on a comprehensive crypto market-structure framework.
items.why: This is a procedural gate rather than passage, but failing to clear 60 would effectively end the bill's 2026 prospects and remove the regulatory-clarity premium that has underpinned institutional allocation all year — and it lands the day before the Fed, so a negative outcome would hit a market already positioned defensively.

items.detail: US spot Bitcoin ETF flows are the tell to watch daily after **$462.6 million of net outflows from September 8 to 11 with zero inflow days**, which cut total ETF assets to roughly $99.33 billion from $103.34 billion on September 3.
items.why: The allocator bid disappearing was what turned last week's rate repricing into a price break, so the first day of net inflows after Wednesday would signal institutions treating the hike as priced-in and cleared, while continued outflows through the decision would leave spot with only leveraged flow to absorb supply.

crossCuttingTheme: Wednesday's FOMC decision and dot plot is the single event all three markets are waiting on — a 25bp hike from 3.50–3.75% is roughly 85–90% priced, so the variable is whether the projections frame the oil-driven inflation impulse as a one-off requiring one move or the start of a series, and that answer sets the Treasury yield path that in turn determines whether the S&P 500 can hold 7,656.98 into Friday's triple witching, whether foreign selling and the 95.55 rupee keep pressuring a Nifty already down five straight weeks, and whether Bitcoin defends $77,000 or loses it toward the bottom of its $75,000–$82,000 range.
